voiceover: Did Jesus really exist — or is he just a myth? Almost no historian agrees with the myth. Believer and atheist alike, scholars treat his existence as settled. Tacitus, a Roman senator, records that Christus was executed under Pontius Pilate. The Jewish historian Josephus mentions Jesus — and the execution of his brother James. Pliny, Suetonius, Lucian, the Talmud — a chain of Roman and Jewish sources corroborate the picture. Even the agnostic scholar Bart Ehrman wrote a whole book refuting the idea that Jesus never existed. And here's the tell: no one invents a crucified messiah. An executed criminal was a scandal, not a marketing plan. You can debate who Jesus was. That he lived is not seriously in doubt.
